newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: New Karachi 100-share index seen more volatile.
newsitem.headline: New Karachi 100-share index seen more volatile.

text.p: The newly-recomposed Karachi 100-share index, in which the state-run telecom utility gets a heavier weighting, is likely to increase market volatility, stocks analysts said on Wednesday.

The Karachi Stock Exchange, which introduced the new index on Tuesday, has increased the weighting of Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd (PTCL) to around 30.64 percent from 6.5 percent, a daily review by KASB & Co said.
PTCL's previous index weighting had represented six billion rupees, or 11.76 percent of its capital. It now represents 3.774 billion PTCL (A) shares, or 74 percent of paid-up capital.
"The market is now too dependent on PTCL," dealer Ather Raouf of Carr Mashriq said. "The recomposed index will increase market volatility."
He said PTCL was fundamentally a weak company and its upside from current levels was very limited.
"In the long run, this heavy weightage of PTCL will not be good for the index and it will limit its upside," he added.
Dealers said two blue chips, PTCL and Hub Power Co Ltd, now account for over 40 percent of the index weight.
The KSE says the recomposed index, based on the prices of April 30, captures about 76 percent of market capitalisation.
Waheed Hasan, an analyst at KASB & Co said PTCL's new weighting had unbalanced the index. "It will not reflect true market sentiment," he added.
Hasan said the index had soared on Tuesday and Wednesday on gains made by PTCL and Hub Power shares. But declining scrips had outnumbered risers, showing a different picture.
The 100-share index surged 27.13 points on Tuesday to end at 1,592.86. But falling stocks beat gainers 216 to 84.
By Wednesday's close the index had risen another 19.49 points to 1,612.35, with 175 losers and 106 advancers.
Khuram Hanif of ING Baring said that despite the debate over the changes the new index would depict the market better.
"PTCL market capitalisation has been accounted for the first time...There could now be fresh buying by index funds," he said.
